chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfaly, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'A time will come upon my community when their inner selves will be foul and their outward appearances beautiful, greedy for the world, and not intending what is with Allah, their Lord. Their religion will become show-off; fear will not mix with them. Allah will encompass them with punishment from it, so they will supplicate to Him with the supplication of the Drowning One, but He will not answer them.'

key_terms.دُعَاءَ الْغَرِيقِ: the supplication of the drowning one

ai.seo_question: What is the state of the community's faith and supplication when they become hypocritical and greedy for the world?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Shia emphasis on 'batin' (inner reality) versus 'zahir' (outer appearance), warning that superficial piety driven by dunya (worldly gain) leads to a state where supplications become ineffective, akin to a drowning person's cry. It underscores the concept of 'riya'' (show-off) as a spiritual disease that severs the connection between the believer and Allah, rendering ritual acts void of acceptance.
